memory_candidates.content: When a repo documents the same underlying quantity under two legitimate but differently-scoped conventions (e.g. primitive-constructor count vs. total-named-schema count including derived mirrors), write the derivation exactly once in a canonical reference file and have every other occurrence link to it with an explicit label, rather than restating or re-deriving the arithmetic per file. Re-typing a corrected figure independently in each file recreates the same drift risk that caused the original staleness.

A stale-count regex tripwire (e.g. check-module-invariants.sh's C14) that requires a specific digit adjacent to a specific word ("axiom"/"constructor"/"schema") is blind to bare numeric claims in table cells or prose that omit the trigger word on the same line (e.g. "| Base | 37 |" or a line-wrapped "45 TM\nschemata"). A green run of such a check is evidence the check didn't fire, not evidence the documented counts are correct — verify by direct comparison against the source of truth (here, Axiom.minFrameClass) rather than trusting the gate's exit code alone.

In a README with a `<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: inventory ... -->` block, only the trailing hand-written description column survives regeneration untouched; every other column (file/line counts) must be refreshed via the project's `--emit-inventory` mechanism after any edit that changes line counts, never hand-patched. Editing adjacent Lean docstrings without re-running the generator leaves the inventory table's counts silently stale.
